subject: CANARY: request for per-route batchable flag and temporary fallback for ACME PoC
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@acme-ai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME PoC — intermittent streaming errors during higher concurrency

Hi Logan,

Quick heads-up from our engineering team running the PoC this morning: when we push concurrency above ~120 QPS the streaming session sometimes fails with a response-id mismatch error, and the client falls back and retries, which doubles latency for the user. We captured a short log snippet (attached) and a terse repro script.

We need a temporary mitigation we can apply while your runtime team digs into a durable fix — ideally something per-route so we don't affect other customers. Is there a way to toggle batching behavior (e.g. force per-request dispatch / disable windowed batching) for just our demo route?

We'd like this change asap — demo with our execs is Friday EOD PT. If you need more info ping Samir (copied).

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform — Acme AI
[attachment: acme_repro_log_snippet.txt (text/plain)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@acme-ai.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME PoC — intermittent streaming errors during higher concurrency

Thanks Elena — sorry you're seeing this in the PoC. We can do a couple of short-term things while platform investigates the root cause:

- Option A (fast): apply a per-route toggle to prefer single-request dispatch (no cross-request batching) for your demo route. This is reversible and low-risk.
- Option B (moderate): route to the smaller compat model for the demo window (trades cost for stability).

I've attached a brief execution plan for the fast toggle (acme-poc-exec-plan.pdf). Karthik, can the runtime team enable a per-route "batch_control=single" flag as a canary for ACME today? If so, we can confirm with Elena and keep it only for the demo window.

Elena/Samir — if you can confirm the exact route name (the PoC is hitting /v1/generate?model=redwood-std-8k&route=acme-poc-demo) and give a 30-min window we can make the change and test with you.

Action items:
- Elena: confirm route name + preferred window
- Karthik: feasibility + rollback plan
- Jonas/Marissa: note for product/pricing so we can log an exception and potential credit if needed

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: acme-poc-exec-plan.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@acme-ai.com>, Samir Patel <samir@acme-ai.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME PoC — intermittent streaming errors during higher concurrency

Thanks Logan and Elena — quick technical note from runtime: the error pattern in the snippet looks like a kv-cache eviction + batching edge where prefetched KV segments are occasionally served to the wrong active stream ID when the per-worker queue flush aligns poorly with interleaved cancels. In short: a race between prefetch + cross-request batching.

Short-term mitigation I can push today (low risk):
- Enable per-route batch_control=single which disables cross-request coalescing on the route and forces immediate dispatch; this should eliminate the mixing that causes response-id mismatches.
- Additionally, enable strict kvcache-validation (extra header checks) for only the acme-poc-demo route for 48 hours to monitor regressions; it increases CPU modestly but is fine for a short demo window.

If you give me the route name and a 30-min window I will:
1) stage the per-route flag in the canary pool (no infra restart).
2) run a quick synthetic at 200 QPS for 10 minutes against the canary.
3) if green, flip the control to live for the PoC traffic window.

Rollback plan: revert the per-route flag (instant) and remove strict kvcache-validation.

I will need: cluster id (from logs) and at least one full request/response trace showing the failure (not just the snippet). Elena, can you share the full trace link or upload to the Drive link Logan included?

-Karthik
Lead Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
